profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer, Full Stack
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary:
I'm a Software Engineer who studied computer science, mathematics & genetics. The curiosity of thought-provoking genetics inspired me to pursue technical background in computer science and molecular genetics. My software problem-solving skills and knowledge of molecular biology allowed me to both generate experimental data and write software to analyze the results. It is incredibly motivating when I look back on the knowledge I have accumulated, to realize how all my areas of expertise can work together to answer questions at the intersection of computer science and biomedical research.

Find out more:
https://edotau.github.io/

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer, Full Stack
positions.description: I lead the technical direction and full-stack delivery of an enterprise in-silico research platform that turns complex computational workflows into intuitive tools for antibody discovery and immunogenicity analysis across multiple therapeutic programs. Day to day I work across React/TypeScript frontends and Django/Celery backends on Kubernetes, with Databricks powering our ML data pipelines and analytics. I built our Databricks infrastructure as code with Terraform and asset bundles spanning dev, QA, and production, and an internal AI-assisted development platform that keeps coding agents authenticated against enterprise model-serving endpoints.
positions.insights: Skills: Biological Data Analysis · Software Infrastructure · Biological Engineering

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer, Full Stack
positions.description: I built full-stack CRISPR diagnostics applications with Django REST Framework and React, including authenticated APIs, webhook integrations, and role-based access control. On the infrastructure side, I modernized our multi-account AWS environment under a single Terraform and CloudFormation infrastructure-as-code strategy, rolled out a cost-optimized EKS cluster running JupyterHub with SSO through AWS Cognito and SAML for the research org, and decoupled async workloads with serverless pipelines on managed queues and pub/sub to improve platform resilience and observability.

positions.title: Software Engineer, DevOps & Infrastructure
positions.description: I led CI/CD platform engineering for our instrument software teams, rolling out GitHub Actions and Jenkins pipelines that shortened release cycles and standardized deployments. I right-sized containerized deployments for single-cell assay pipelines to cut cloud costs, and built data ingestion services and Go data-wrangling pipelines that turned high-volume single-cell assay streams into clean, structured datasets for downstream analytics and model training. I also led SARS-CoV-2 genomic surveillance efforts, designing the sequencing strategy and custom analysis pipelines that identified the CAL.20C variant.

positions.title: Software Engineer, Data Scientist
positions.description:
The power of interdisciplinary knowledge was on full display when we used cutting-edge genomic sequencing technologies to uncover molecular genetic changes in stickleback fish that are associated with adaptive evolution. I led this research project which included identifying and collecting samples, performing DNA extractions, ligated sequencing adapters onto billions of DNA fragments, and using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) to generate DNA constructs suitable for sequencing. 

After generating sequencing datasets, I leveraged my computer science background to write software to provide new insights into stickleback biology. Genetic variants, especially large segments of DNA, are heavily penalized by the alignment algorithm and result in variant reads being reported as unaligned—throwing away true biological information. We worked to implement a computational framework to represent all common alleles within the reference genome to improve our read mapping capability and downstream analyses. The computational model represents the reference genome as a graph where nodes are genomic segments, edges represent the order and orientation of these segments, and a path through the graph represents a possible allelic variation. The graph is a fundamental concept learned in computer science and can be a powerful tool when applied to genetics. Modeling genomes as a graph to represent all common alleles improves genome diversity by incorporating genetic elements from multiple populations, a fundamental and impactful change to the way genetics is carried out.

positions.title: Senior Research Analyst
positions.description: I managed mRNA-Seq analysis on responses to physical activity from a cohort resulted in a comprehensive molecular map that accelerated the development of therapeutics and exercise recommendations. I developed sequencing data transfers from local servers to Azure Cloud and established cloud computing infrastructure that ensured fast data delivery to collaborators and clients. I designed DNA/RNA isolation assays at production scale which optimized workflow and reduced cost.

positions.title: Senior Lab Technician
positions.description: I was responsible for replenishing supplies and basic molecular biology experiments to increase efficiency and quality of all laboratory operations
